Guidance: Methods used to gather stakeholder needs including interviews, focus groups, and surveys.
Analytical processes applied to structure, clarify, and model requirements.
Strategy for maintaining active stakeholder participation throughout requirements definition.
Classification scheme covering business, stakeholder, solution, functional, and non-functional requirements.
Formatting guidelines and documentation artifacts used to record verified requirements.
Ranking methodology (such as MoSCoW, weighted scoring, or value ranking) to prioritize scope.
Quantitative metrics measuring requirements volatility, defect density, and coverage.
Attributes and linkages tracked across the requirements lifecycle to ensure bidirectional traceability.
Procedures for baseline versioning and evaluating changes to documented requirements.
Techniques ensuring requirements are complete, consistent, unambiguous, and testable.
Approach for validating that final deliverables fulfill underlying business objectives.
